No atoms are lost or made, so total mass stays the same.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acid: donates H+ (pH < 7).

Alkali: dissolves to give OH-.

Neutralisation: H+ + OH- -> H2O.

HCl + NaOH -> NaCl + H2O.

H2SO4 -> sulfate; HNO3 -> nitrate.

Balance equations: same atoms each side.

Mass before = mass after, including any gas.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.
A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
